meta.title: DIMS — stylometric analysis of coordinated publications
meta.description: DIMS compares the writing style of texts from different channels and sites using Burrows' Delta and shows which publications follow the same template. An integrated risk score R_DIMS and a grade from F to SSS.

problem.title: A coordinated campaign gives itself away through style, not topic
problem.p1: When several channels post the same text with minor edits, checking each post separately takes hours. A shared topic proves nothing on its own: everyone writes about the same event.
problem.p2: Stylometry compares the frequencies of the most common words. This fingerprint barely depends on the topic and survives reordering and word swaps, so a shared template or a shared author shows up within seconds.

how.title: Three steps from sources to report

steps.title: Add sources
steps.text: TXT, PDF, DOCX, RTF and HTML files, article links or pasted text. Or collect material through Google News, RSS feeds and public Telegram channels.

steps.title: Run the analysis
steps.text: DIMS computes the Burrows' Delta distance for every pair of texts, builds a dendrogram, a heatmap and a projection of sources, and flags pairs below the θΔ threshold.

steps.title: Get the report
steps.text: An integrated R_DIMS score, a grade from F to SSS, confidence intervals for every pair and a report ready to print or save as PDF.

method.title: One score, five explainable indicators
method.lead: Stylometric similarity is only one signal. DIMS weighs five indicators and shows the contribution of each, so the analyst can see where the score comes from.

limits.title: Limits of the method
entries: Stylometric similarity is an indicator, not proof. A low Δ can mean a shared author, a shared template or simply the same genre. In the demo set, two independent news reports also scored Δ = 0.44.
Reliable results need texts of 500 words or more. DIMS flags shorter ones with a warning.
All-word analysis works with any language. Function-word mode currently supports Ukrainian, Russian and English.
A person decides whether something is disinformation, after checking the facts and the context.
limits.source_text: The method builds on Burrows' Delta and was developed as part of doctoral research in information systems and technologies.
limits.citation: Burrows, J. (2002). ‘Delta’: a Measure of Stylistic Difference and a Guide to Likely Authorship. Literary and Linguistic Computing, 17(3), 267–287.

entries.q: Does DIMS prove that a text is disinformation?
entries.a: No. DIMS shows stylistic similarity and an overall risk level. A person draws the conclusion after checking the facts and the context.
All-word analysis works with any language that separates words with spaces. Function-word mode currently supports Ukrainian, Russian and English. Compare texts written in the same language.
